conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Agent Harris with the IRS Taxpayer Services Department. I'm calling regarding your eligibility for a federal tax stimulus refund. May I confirm that I'm speaking with Mrs. Jeanette Williams?
Yes, this is Jeanette Williams. What is this about?

Thank you, Mrs. Williams. According to our records, you may be entitled to a special IRS refund due to an adjustment in your 2022 tax filings. Have you received a notice in the mail regarding this matter?
No, I haven't seen anything in the mail yet. Is this about my Social Security or Medicare?

It is related to your tax status, which may impact your Social Security benefits if not addressed promptly. To proceed with disbursing your stimulus refund, we must first verify your identity under federal guidelines.
Oh dear, I can't afford to lose my benefits. What do I need to do?

First, please be advised that this is a time-sensitive matter. If we cannot complete verification today, your eligibility for the refund could be rescinded, and there may be a delay or hold on your benefits.
I really can't have any delay. My budget is very tight. Please help me.
I understand entirely, Mrs. Williams. To comply with IRS regulations, there is a mandatory identity-confirmation fee of $297, which is fully refundable and required before we release your payment.
I have to pay a fee? Can't that be taken out of the refund?

Unfortunately, IRS policy requires the identity-verification fee to be paid upfront to prevent fraudulent claims. Once verified, your full refund of $1,534 will be processed to your account within 24 hours.
I'm not sure I understand. If I don't pay this today, what will happen?

If the fee is not received today, IRS procedures require us to report the unverified status, which could result in a temporary freeze on your Social Security disbursements and possible late penalties.
Oh my goodness, I can't have that happen. How do I pay the fee?
For your convenience and security, we currently accept payment through Zelle, Cash App, or direct wire transfer. Which method would you prefer to use?
I suppose I could use Zelle. I've used that for my grandson before.
Very good. Please open your Zelle app, and I will provide you the IRS processing address. Are you ready to write this down?
Yes, I'm ready.
Please enter the following email in the recipient field: refund.verification@irs-usa-gov.com. The amount is $297. In the note section, write your full name and 'ID Verification Fee'.
Alright, I'm entering it now. Are you sure this is the right way?

Absolutely, Mrs. Williams. This is the standard IRS secure payment channel. Once received, I will immediately confirm your identity and process your refund. If you encounter any issues or fail to complete this today, please be aware that your account may be flagged for further review.
Okay, I'll send it now. I really hope I don't lose my Social Security.
Thank you for your prompt cooperation. Please notify me once the payment has been sent so I can expedite your refund approval.
